note: Why a running gateway would not retire when a newer Nessa asked it to, said in the one way that survives the process boundary (ADR 221). The gateway writes one of these names as `refusal` in `gateway-upgrade/result.json` whenever `retired` is false, and the desktop host decides what to do from the name alone, never from the free-form `cleanupError` beside it. `data_missing`: the gateway's stops failed, but nothing it started still holds resources (no agent whose release is unconfirmed or whose provider open is in flight, no unsettled opening, no deletion still stopping its process, no warm-up scheduled or holding its agent), and its conversation data is no longer where it was opened; the host may stop the gateway itself, recording that it did. `not_confirmed`: anything else that could not be confirmed; the host fails the attempt and Try again asks again. A result with no `refusal` comes from a gateway that predates this file and is read as `not_confirmed`. A new name needs its row in ADR 221 first.
